question: remove_brigade end to end for OpenHOI3: the one-regiment arm, the hourly drain, RemoveUnit's officers and children; add_division's starting strength

addresses.name: CRemoveBrigadeEffect::Execute
addresses.signature: void __thiscall CRemoveBrigadeEffect::Execute(CRemoveBrigadeEffect* this, CEventScope* scope, int unused)
addresses.comment: **`remove_brigade`, 6,881 live instances, and what it matches on is not the brigade type.** 0x5BBF10 to the last of three `ret 8` exits, at rvas 0x5BC030, 0x5BC133 and 0x5BC1DB; CRemoveBrigadeEffect::GetText begins at 0x5BC1E0, which is what says the third `ret` really is the end (trap 3's vftable check). It walks the scope country's `units (CCountry +0xBAC)` and, inside each, the unit's `regiments (CUnit +0x38)`, asking each regiment for **slot 8** - a folded body (rva 0x6C6C50, five holders including CEU3DialogGuiType, so it stays unnamed) that returns a copy of `CSubUnit +0x68`, which project.json already names **`name`, the historical regiment name** - and comparing it for exact equality with the effect's own `CStringEffect::text (+0x20)`. The comparison is a plain memcmp plus a length test, so it is **case-sensitive**, unlike the flag trees. **On the first match in the whole country it stops**, and: if the unit holds more than one regiment (`regiments_count +0x40 != 1`) it calls the already-recorded `RemoveRegimentFromUnit` (rva 0x1BE9A0) and then rva 0x284CE0(game state, regiment), which disposes of the regiment (not read); if the regiment is the unit's only one it pushes **the unit's persistent id (`CUnit +0x10/+0x14`) onto `CGameState::pending_unit_removals (+0xBF4)`** with the queue's own `lock xadd` - so the whole unit is removed later, on the tick thread, when RunHourlyTick drains the queue through CGameState::RemoveUnit. **Corrected 2026-10-12: that path was described as a localisation render and a message; there is neither - what looked like one is the inlined get-or-create of the game state singleton.** **Read again 2026-11-16 for OpenHOI3's build of it** (FINDINGS-effectrun.md, section 3.11): the walk is the country's +0xBAC list node by node (+0 the unit, +8 the next) and each unit's +0x38 regiments the same way, so the first match in list order wins; the one-regiment test is `regiments_count (+0x40) == 1` (0x9BC045). In that arm the regiment is **not** taken out of its unit, so a second `remove_brigade` of the same name before the hour ends finds the same regiment and queues the same unit again - which the drain passes over (CGameState::QueueUnitRemoval). Neither arm touches officers or manpower; the unit's officers go in the drain's RemoveUnit. The other arm hands the unit to RemoveRegimentFromUnit in EDI (0x9BC033 loads it) and the regiment to CGameState::DisposeSubUnit, which keeps a ship on the sunk list (+0x20) - so a ship removed so counts for total_of_ours_sunk.

addresses.name: CGameState::QueueUnitRemoval
addresses.comment:
**How a TBB worker gets a unit deleted without deleting it.** Thirty instructions: copy the object's id pair (`+0x10`, `+0x14`) to the stack, `lock xadd` the tail counter of the `tbb::concurrent_queue` at `CCurrentGameState +0xBF4`, and push the pair into the micro-queue that ticket selects. The object arrives in **EAX**, the state is the one stack argument, `ret 4` at `0x684CDA`.

Eight callers, and the first two are the ones that matter for hooking: `0x5B9F0C` and `0x5B9FE7` are inside **`CUnit::UpdateHourly`**, which runs on a TBB worker. `0x5BA4C8` and `0x5BA714` are inside `CUnit::CheckOrderAndCombat` (tick thread), `0x5D0D8F` is in `CAir::UpdateDaily`, `0x5D0443`, `0x5CA7CB` and `0x8ABBE8` are the rest. Nothing on this path frees anything: the queue is drained on the tick thread at the end of `RunHourlyTick`. **The drain, read 2026-11-16** (0x682230-0x6822B7, FINDINGS-effectrun.md section 3.11): each popped pair is looked up through 0xA9DA00 in the database its type selects ([0x1A857F4] at or under 0x1268, else [0x1A857F0]); a pair that no longer resolves - a unit already removed - is passed over (`test eax,eax; je` at 0x6822A1 and again after the -8 at 0x6822A8), and a live one goes to CGameState::RemoveUnit(state, unit, 0, 1) (`push 1; push ebx(0); push eax` at 0x6822AC). So a unit queued twice in one hour is removed once, with its officers lost and its passengers removed with it.

addresses.name: CGameState::RemoveUnit
addresses.signature: void __thiscall CGameState::RemoveUnit(CGameState* this, CUnit* unit, bool keepOfficers, bool withPassengers)
addresses.comment:
**A unit ceases to exist**, and this is where it is destroyed.

It unlinks the unit from everything holding it - its country's units, its province, its parent's Children in the order of battle, plans and orders, the interface's selection - takes its regiments off it through RemoveRegimentFromUnit, and then calls **the unit's own scalar deleting destructor**, `unit->vftable->vf_0(1)`. So the object is freed, not handed on.

**The units under it** (+0x1E4): after CUnit::LeaveAllCombats and CUnit_LeaveParent(unit, true), each child in turn is CUnit_LeaveParent(child, true) - left at the top of the order of battle, **not handed to the removed unit's superior** - and where the removed unit is a theatre (oob_level 0) the child's `orphaned` (+0x50) is set. A fleet's children are its carriers' air groups, so a fleet merged into another (CMergeCommand::Execute: CUnit_MergeInto, then this) leaves the groups aboard the ships that went over with nobody above them.

Its callers are every place a unit is gone for good: a country capitulating or being annexed with units it cannot transfer, CDisbandCommand::Execute, and CUnit::RetreatFromCombat finding nowhere to retreat to.

**The two flags.** With the first clear, the owner's officers fall by the unit's officers times its strength share times the officer ratio, floored at nought. The second decides what becomes of what the unit carries: **a fleet's land units and an air unit's land units alike** are removed with it (RemoveUnit called on each with the same flags) where it is set, and otherwise let go where they stand - a fleet's passengers with +0x300, +0x1C8, +0x2E4 and +0x2E8 cleared, an air unit's with +0x304 and +0x2E8 - with no supplies moved and no battle looked for. The hourly removal drain, a capitulation and an annexation, and a disbanded rebel army pass it set (each recorded at its call); the government-in-exile clean-up passes it clear for a unit it destroys outright; CCountry_Reset's call was not read. So **a transport plane destroyed takes its paratroopers with it**. A land unit removed is taken off its fleet's or its plane's list. A fleet removed also lets go each carrier's air groups - out of the fleet in the order of battle, off the ship's list, a fresh null order, CAir::CheckBase and CUnit::EnterProvince where they stand - before each ship goes to DisposeSubUnit. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-transport.md, sections A.5, D.1 and D.3, and FINDINGS-transport.md, section D.1 (the order of battle). **The officers, read off the listing 2026-11-16** (0x684E87-0x684F7C, FINDINGS-effectrun.md section 3.11): skipped where the first flag is set; otherwise O = the sum over the unit's regiments of their definition's `officers` (+0x58 -> +0x118), S = the sum of their `strength` (+0x5C), M = slot 23 GetTotalMaxStrength; nothing where M <= 0; else share = S x 1000 / M (64-bit, __allmul/__alldiv, cut to 32 bits), lost = share x O / 1000, and **the country charged is the expeditionary owner where +0x290 is set, else the owner** (+0x28C or +0x124 through the tag lookup 0x402610): its officers (+0xC4) fall by lost x OfficerRatio (+0xD4) / 1000, floored at 0. So a lent unit removed costs its lender the officers, not its host. The children loop (0x684FEE-0x685014) was checked on the same listing: CUnit_LeaveParent(child, 1) for each, `orphaned` (+0x50) set where the removed unit's oob_level (+0x1F4) is 0.

addresses.name: CAddDivisionEffect::Execute
addresses.signature: void __thiscall CAddDivisionEffect::Execute(CAddDivisionEffect* this, CEventScope* scope, int unknown)
addresses.comment: **Slot 11, what `add_division` does.** Takes the province from the effect's +0x3C through g_CMap +0x2200 and the owner from the scope's country, falling back to the province's controller (+0x334/+0x338). Then walks the {definition, name} entries the loader collected at +0x40/+0x44 and, for the first one, allocates the parent unit too - **the class coming from the brigade definition's own flags**: land (+0x2D) gives CRegiment 0xD8 under CArmy 0x308, is_air (+0x2C) CWing under CAir 0x2F4, anything else CShip 0xF8 under CNavy 0x2FC. Each object gets an id from the generator at 0x170AF78 with type 0x29, its type through CSubUnit::SetType, its name from the entry's string, and its organisation from CSubUnit::GetMaxOrganisation; then CUnit::EnterProvince puts the unit **on the map** - not in the deployment pool - and, only where CCurrentGameState +0xD0C is set and the scope's country is the player's, CEU3AI_SortUnitsIntoTheatres(its CEU3AI, 1) at 0x5B5DD5 puts its units under the theatres they stand in (FINDINGS-agents.md G; the record had this call as a notice to the player). See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-oob.md. Signature corrected 2026-10-02 by the signature audit (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-sigaudit.md). **The brigade's strength, seen 2026-11-16 and not read further** (0x9B5AB1-0x9B5B03, FINDINGS-effectrun.md section 3.11): slot 12 GetMaxStrength is called twice on the new sub unit, with (1, 0) and with (0, 0), and `strength` (+0x5C) is the smaller of the two, floored at 0, with `strength_ceiling` (+0x30) raised to it; then the organisation through CSubUnit::GetMaxOrganisation (0x5AB700) with (1, 0). What the two flags of GetMaxStrength mean was not read, so whether a reserve brigade starts held down is open. `home` (+0x64) is set just before. OpenHOI3 leaves add_division unbuilt: neither Their Finest Hour nor BlackICE uses it.
